{"items": ["[passage_read_so_far]
- Utterson and Enfield take their Sunday walk down a by-street.（Mr. Utterson、Mr. Richard Enfield）
- Enfield points his cane at a sinister door and asks Utterson if he ever remarked it.（Mr. Richard Enfield、Mr. Utterson）
- Enfield says the door is connected with a very odd story.（Mr. Richard Enfield）
- The man tramples over the girl's body and leaves her screaming.（the man in the middle、the screaming child）
- Enfield collars the man and brings him back to the group around the child.（Mr. Richard Enfield、the man in the middle）
- The doctor turns sick and white with desire to kill the prisoner.（the Sawbones、the man in the middle）
- They threaten scandal and force the man to pay a hundred pounds.（Mr. Richard Enfield、the man in the middle）
- The man leads them to the door, unlocks it, and returns with gold and a cheque.（the man in the middle）
- The man offers to stay until the banks open and cash the cheque himself.（Mr. Richard Enfield、the man in the middle）
- They spend the night in Enfield's chambers and go to the bank next day.（Mr. Richard Enfield、the man in the middle）
- Enfield presents the cheque believing it a forgery, but it proves genuine.（Mr. Richard Enfield）
- Enfield calls the door place Black Mail House and muses.（Mr. Richard Enfield、Mr. Utterson）
- Utterson asks if the cheque drawer lives there.（Mr. Utterson、Mr. Richard Enfield）
- Enfield says he noticed the drawer's address in some square.（Mr. Richard Enfield）
- Enfield explains his rule of not asking questions.（Mr. Richard Enfield）
- Enfield describes the door house: no other door, clean shut windows, smoking chimney.（Mr. Richard Enfield）
- Utterson asks the name of the man who walked over the child.（Mr. Utterson、Mr. Richard Enfield）
- Enfield names the man as Hyde.（Mr. Richard Enfield）
- Enfield describes Hyde as deformed and detestable.（Mr. Richard Enfield）
- Utterson asks if Hyde used a key.（Mr. Utterson、Mr. Richard Enfield）
- Utterson says he already knows the other party's name.（Mr. Utterson、Mr. Richard Enfield）
- Enfield confirms Hyde still has the key and used it a week ago.（Mr. Richard Enfield）
- Enfield and Utterson agree never to refer to the matter again.（Mr. Richard Enfield、Mr. Utterson）

[note_g1]
During a Sunday walk, Utterson and Enfield stop at a sinister door. Enfield recalls a story: a man trampled a girl, then paid her family £100 with a cheque. The cheque proved genuine. Enfield names the man Hyde, deformed and detestable, who still holds the key. Utterson says he knows the other party’s name.
